title: Zeroth two-term cohomology is invariants
statement: Let l be prime, A a finite ring, and C the category of discrete continuous A-linear representations of the additive l-adic integers [def-exc-discrete-modules-category, def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Let V:C -> A-Mod be any functor equipped with linear equivalences t_M:V(M) -> intersection_g ker(rho_M(g)-id), natural in the underlying coefficient maps. Let K be the explicit action complex [def-exc-action-two-term-complex] with tau=1. Then H^0(K(-)) is naturally isomorphic to V.

source.place: First paragraph, identification of the degree-zero kernel with invariants

proof.text: The coinduced embedding makes each orbit map locally constant. If tau fixes m, induction shows every nonnegative integer fixes m. Mathlib PadicInt.denseRange_natCast and continuity of the orbit map into the discrete module imply every l-adic integer fixes m. The converse is immediate.

Compose t_M with the invariant-submodule inclusion. This is injective and its image is the kernel of rho(tau)-id by the preceding fixed-vector equivalence. ModuleCat.isLimitKernelFork identifies this kernel with K(M).cycles 0. No differential enters degree zero, so CochainComplex.isoHomologyπ₀ identifies cycles and homology.
For a coefficient map, naturality of t and the cycles inclusion show equality after composition with the invariant inclusion. That inclusion is monic, giving naturality of the homology isomorphisms.
